commits.message: Review fixes: visual order resolves the raw line, edges follow a stated direction, the cut trims spans as Rich does, wrap refuses visual at runtime, render draws drafts (rich-unfiled-791c.8khi)
A text's wrapped rows are public as RichText, spans intact, and render draws them (rich-unfiled-791c.8khi)
A loop's drawn step is its unsnapped step plus one level: 96 levels, shimmer 149 s, sparkle 163 s keep every loop under 0.04 over the hour grid (rich-animation-42lg.twz)
The contrast settling checks through drawnAt too, and a share is always stated (rich-animation-42lg.twz)
The loops test measures through drawnAt, the renderer's own draw step, not a copy of it (rich-animation-42lg.twz)
Pulse and shimmer stay under the 0.04 bar as drawn: the loops test measures the snapped field, and the two loops slow to 53 s and 127 s (rich-animation-42lg.twz)

CI runs the newest peer version a consumer's install resolves (rich-unfiled-791c.7kj7) (#545)

* CI installs the tarball beside each peer's newest in-range version and renders through it (rich-unfiled-791c.7kj7)

The node-floor action becomes .github/actions/consumer with an end input:
floor keeps the lowest Node and locked peers; ceiling names each optional
peer by its peerDependencies range so npm resolves the newest, as a
consumer's install does. One planner, one probe reading the plan; the probe
now renders through each peer-backed subpath (a Checkbox toggled through a
mobx action, a template through go-template-js), so the floor end exercises
mobx too. ci.yml and publish.yml run it as one matrix job over both ends.

Verified locally: ceiling resolved mobx 7.1.4 and passed; floor passed on a
real Node 20.0.0; a broken expectation fails the probe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
